facts: Step definitions are plain functions decorated with `@given`, `@when` or `@then`, imported from `behave` (`from behave import given, when, then`). behave loads every module under `features/steps/`; the Given/When/Then keyword is irrelevant to matching.

Step parameters are captured by the default `parse` matcher with `{name}` or `{name:Type}` placeholders (`@then('the paragraph has {count:d} runs')`). For regular expressions call `use_step_matcher('re')` first, and switch back with `use_step_matcher('parse')` -- the setting applies to every step defined after it.
To convert a captured string into an object, register a type with `behave.register_type(Bool=parse_bool)` and name it in the placeholder (`{value:Bool}`). There is no separate transform decorator.
The scenario's `Background` steps run before it and need definitions too.
`features/environment.py` holds the lifecycle hooks (`before_all`, `before_feature`, `before_scenario`, and their `after_` counterparts). It is retained: do not write one.

The `context` object passed to every step is the shared state between steps of a scenario (`context.document = document`, then read `context.document` in a later step). behave resets it per scenario; anything that must outlive a scenario belongs on `context.config` or in the environment hooks.
Assertions are plain `assert` statements. behave reports the AssertionError as the step failure, so include a message (`assert len(paragraphs) == 3, "got %d" % len(paragraphs)`).

In the execution repository, the library under test is imported as `docx` and lives in `src/docx/`; `src` is already on the import path, so `from docx import Document` works without installing anything. Production code is never accepted.

The `.docx`, `.jpg`, `.png`, `.bmp`, `.gif`, `.tif`, `.emf` and `.wmf` fixtures a scenario opens are still on disk in `features/steps/test_files/`, and their names are the ones the scenario text uses. The helper module that used to turn a name into a path went with the removed code; write whatever helper you need, or build the path directly.
A scenario that SAVES a document writes into `features/_scratch/`, which the retained environment hook creates before the run. Nothing else in the tree may be written.

This workspace supports reading, searching, editing, and syntax parsing. It is a provisioned application runtime for the code in `./repo`; nothing here is executed by the harness. The harness executes your final submitted test artifacts against a separate, complete implementation after generation ends. You receive no harness execution feedback during generation.
TARGET_CONTRACTS.md contains the reviewed public API and configuration supplement supplied in every visibility view. It is context for writing tests; edits to it are not submitted.
Implementation visibility: the reviewed target bodies, including behavior-bearing delegated helpers, are hidden; declarations and permitted surrounding implementations remain visible.
environment.platform: the python-docx library for reading and writing Word .docx files (Python 3.12, lxml)
environment.retained: the retained `features/environment.py` hooks and the `features/steps/test_files/` fixtures

rules: Only files under `repo/features/steps/` are accepted. Repo-wide removal deleted those directories, so create whatever path you need; `features/environment.py` and the fixtures in `features/steps/test_files/` are what remain.
Production code is never accepted. Anything you change outside `repo/features/steps/` is discarded.
